title: Iceberg Quantum Validates Pinnacle 1.2 Architecture with Crevasse QLDPC Decoder to Reduce RSA-2048 Factoring Resources - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Fault-tolerant quantum architecture startup Iceberg Quantum has released Pinnacle 1.2, demonstrating direct circuit-level simulations of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes that validate logical error rates below 10-12 per logical qubit-cycle—the threshold required to execute 2048-bit RSA integer factorization.

The breakthrough is enabled by Crevasse, Iceberg Quantum’s new QLDPC decoder. Crevasse achieves an average decoding latency of 4 microseconds per error-correction round, enabling the team to execute trillions of simulated error-correction cycles directly rather than relying on statistical extrapolations. By combining Crevasse’s decoding efficiency with compiled modular exponentiation circuits, Iceberg Quantum updated its resource estimates for breaking RSA-2048 to 72,000 physical qubits in 3.7 days at a physical error rate of p = 10-3 (and 48,000 physical qubits in 0.98 days at p = 10-4 for a 1-microsecond code cycle time), representing a significant reduction in spacetime overhead compared to Pinnacle 1.0.

Direct Error-Correction Sampling and Circuit Compilation

To establish these metrics, Iceberg Quantum simulated one trillion samples across Pinnacle memory and processing blocks without encountering logical failures under smaller code distances: observing only three logical errors on its d = 16 ([[254,14,16]]) code at p = 10-3 (a logical error rate of 2 × 10-13) and zero logical errors on its d = 10 ([[126,12,10]]) code at p = 10-4 (≤ 3 × 10-13). The use of smaller code distances reduces spatial overhead by ~40% and temporal overhead by ~30% compared to Pinnacle 1.0 benchmarks.

The team verified complete modular exponentiation circuits against models of the Pinnacle architecture using forced-gap post-selection for state injection into magic state distillation blocks, achieving injection error rates of (1.3 ± 0.3) × 10-6 (d = 10) and producing output magic states with failure rates near pout ≈ 3.5 × 10-11. Applied to Frozen Pinnacle—a variant designed for fixed 8-degree connectivity superconducting systems—the improved compilation reduces resource requirements to 99,000 physical qubits and a 5.0-day execution runtime.
